title: Do Teachers Dream of GenAI Widening Educational (In)equality? Envisioning the Future of K-12 GenAI Education from Global Teachers’ Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with K-12 teachers, capturing educators' accounts of infrastructural divides, lack of reliable internet, and differing baseline digital literacies among students from different economic backgrounds.

Qualitative analysis of teachers' observations regarding GenAI outputs defaulting to Western-centric perspectives or dominant cultural narratives (e.g., misrepresenting Taiwanese indigenous cultures or South African contexts).

Qualitative interviews capturing teachers' reports on GenAI systems defaulting to dominant language variants (e.g., Mainland Chinese expressions over Taiwanese Mandarin) and failing to recognize local linguistic identities.

Thematic analysis of educators' experiences with AI models generating racially skewed outputs, such as defaulting to white figures for successful scientists and producing stereotyped imagery of Black individuals.

Qualitative accounts from special education teachers evaluating the lack of accessibility features in GenAI user interfaces (e.g., small font sizes, excessive steps, poor color options) that exclude students with learning or intellectual disabilities.
